criteria.text: The participant has a pathologically confirmed malignancy for which high-dose rate brachytherapy is appropriate as a component of their therapeutic regimen.
The participant is greater than 18 years of age.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0, 1, or 2.

The participant has a primary medical or surgical oncologist in the community or at National Cancer Institute (NCI) who is willing to collaborate with the Radiation Oncology Branch (ROB) staff in the clinical management of the participant.

The participant is of childbearing or child-fathering potential and is willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control, which includes abstinence, while they are being treated on this study.
The participant has endometrial cancer.

The participant is at a higher risk of recurrence (because of either grade, myometrial invasion, lymphatic vascular space invasion, tumor size, lymph node status, tumor extension, presence or absence of surgical staging).
The participant has suffered a recurrence at the vaginal cuff.
The participant is unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary endometrial cancer.
The participant has cervical cancer.
The participant is unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary cervical cancer.

The participant has locally advanced cervical cancer in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation either in a palliative or curative setting (definitive or post-operative setting).
The participant has lung cancer.
The participant has an endobronchial component causing symptoms.
The participant cannot undergo resection because of poor lung function or distant lung metastasis.
The participant has breast cancer.
The participant has infiltrating ductal carcinoma or ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS), stage T0, T1, and T2 less than or equal to 3.0 cm, N0 and M0.
The participant is benefiting from high dose radiation (HDR) as either as a boost or accelerated partial breast irradiation regimen.
The participant has prostate cancer.
The participant has localized prostate cancer (T1b-T3b) in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation or used as monotherapy for definitive management.
The participant is cognitively impaired and cannot give informed consent.
The participant is currently receiving concurrent investigational chemotherapeutic agents.

The participant is receiving concomitant chemotherapy administration in the 5 days preceding brachytherapy (except for gynecological cancer patients who may have received concurrent chemotherapy as a component of their treatment regimen).
The participant is pregnant or breast-feeding.

The participant has a clinically significant unrelated systemic illness (serious infections or significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic or other organ dysfunction), which in the judgment of the Principal or Associate Investigator would compromise the participant s ability to tolerate this therapy or are likely to interfere with the study procedures or results.
The participant is deemed unable or unlikely to adhere to protocol treatment.
The participant has abnormal bleeding times or active anti-coagulation therapy.
The participant has platelets less than 100,000 per mm(3).
The participant has Prothrombin time (PT)/Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) greater than 1.5 the upper normal limit (UNL).

The participant or tumor/anatomical factors may prevent brachytherapy apparatus from being properly and safely inserted and positioned and from radiation therapy being administered per American Brachytherapy Society (ABS) guidelines.
The participant has breast cancer.
The participant is inappropriate for standard breast conservation therapy (Multicentric disease, inability to achieve clear margins).
The participant is a male with breast cancer.
The participant has autoimmune disorders, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Scleroderma, etc.
The participant has distant metastases.
The participant has prostate cancer.
The participant has distant metastases.
The participant has lymph node metastases.

P1.text: Pathologically confirmed malignancy for which high-dose rate brachytherapy is appropriate as a component of their therapeutic regimen.

P2.text: Age greater than 18 years of age.

P3.text: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0, 1, or 2.

P4.text: Participant must have a primary medical or surgical oncologist in the community or at National Cancer Institute (NCI) who is willing to collaborate with the Radiation Oncology Branch (ROB) staff in the clinical management of the participant.

P5.text: Participants of childbearing or child- fathering potential must be willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control, which includes abstinence, while they are being treated on this study.

P7.text: Participants at a higher risk of recurrence (because of either grade, myometrial invasion, lymphatic vascular space invasion, tumor size, lymph node status, tumor extension, presence or absence of surgical staging)

P8.text: Participants who have suffered a recurrence at the vaginal cuff

P9.text: Participants who are unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary endometrial cancer.

P11.text: Participants who are unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary cervical cancer.

P12.text: Participants with locally advanced cervical cancer in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation either in a palliative or curative setting (definitive or post-operative setting).

P14.text: Participants with an endobronchial component causing symptoms

P15.text: Participants who cannot undergo resection because of poor lung function or distant lung metastasis

P17.text: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma or ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS), stage T0, T1, and T2 less than or equal to 3.0 cm, N0 and M0,

P18.text: Participants benefiting from high dose radiation (HDR) as either as a boost or accelerated partial breast irradiation regimen.

P20.text: -Participants with localized prostate cancer (T1b-T3b) in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation or used as monotherapy for definitive management.

P21.text: Cognitively impaired participants who cannot give informed consent.

P22.text: Participants currently receiving concurrent investigational chemotherapeutic agents.

P23.text: Participants receiving concomitant chemotherapy administration in the 5 days preceding brachytherapy (except for gynecological cancer patients who may have received concurrent chemotherapy as a component of their treatment regimen)

P24.text: Pregnant or breast-feeding females are excluded because of the potential mutagenic effects on a developing fetus or newborn.

P25.text: Clinically significant unrelated systemic illness (serious infections or significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic or other organ dysfunction), which in the judgment of the Principal or Associate Investigator would compromise the participant s ability to tolerate this therapy or are likely to interfere with the study procedures or results.

P26.text: Participants who are in the estimation of the PI, deemed unable or unlikely to adhere to protocol treatment.

P27.text: Abnormal bleeding times or active anti-coagulation therapy.

P29.text: Prothrombin time (PT)/Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) greater than 1.5 the upper normal limit (UNL)

P30.text: Any participant or tumor/anatomical factors that may prevent brachytherapy apparatus from being properly and safely inserted and positioned and from radiation therapy being administered per American Brachytherapy Society (ABS) guidelines.

P32.text: Participants inappropriate for standard breast conservation therapy (Multicentric disease, inability to achieve clear margins);

P34.text: autoimmune disorders, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Scleroderma, etc.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study of Patients Receiving High-Dose Rate Brachytherapy". I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with a cancer for which high-dose rate brachytherapy (a type of internal radiation therapy) is considered an appropriate part of your treatment plan?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if that's appropriate for me. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium, and I've had a hysterectomy, but I'm not sure if brachytherapy is part of the plan for my current situation with liver lesions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The trial asks about this: “The participant is greater than 18 years of age.”. Does this describe you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 65 years old, so I am definitely greater than 18.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know your ECOG performance status? It's a score from 0 to 2 that measures how well you can do usual daily activities. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My ECOG performance status is 1. I am restricted in physically strenuous activity but I am ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a primary medical or surgical oncologist (in the community or at NCI) who is willing to work with the study's Radiation Oncology team to manage your care?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a specific oncologist willing to work with their Radiation Oncology team. I have been seeing doctors for my chemotherapy and surgeries, but I haven't discussed this trial arrangement with them.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, do you currently have a primary oncologist (medical or surgical) who is willing to coordinate with the study's Radiation Oncology team for your care?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my current doctors are willing to coordinate with a Radiation Oncology team for this trial. I haven't discussed this specific arrangement with them yet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently of childbearing or child-fathering potential? This means you could potentially become pregnant or father a child.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am 65 years old, so I am not of childbearing potential.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your pathology results (like tumor grade, size, or spread), do you know if your doctor considers you at a higher risk of the cancer returning?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my doctor considers me at higher risk for recurrence based on specific pathology details like grade or size. I do know that my cancer has progressed with new liver lesions and lymphadenopathy despite treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us assess your risk, do you know if your cancer involved the lymph nodes, spread beyond the uterus, or was a higher grade (more aggressive type)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my cancer involved the lymph nodes, as sentinel nodes were taken. It also spread beyond the uterus to the liver and lymph nodes, which is why it is stage M1.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a recurrence of cancer specifically at the vaginal cuff?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a recurrence at the vaginal cuff. My records show progression in the liver and lymph nodes, but I haven't been told about any specific recurrence at the vaginal cuff.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by your doctor that you are unable to undergo surgery for your primary endometrial cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have already had surgery for my primary cancer. I had a robotic hysterectomy and pelvic node dissection back in May 2021.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, was your original cancer diagnosed as cervical cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, my original cancer was diagnosed as serous carcinoma of the endometrium, not cervical cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since your original cancer was endometrial, not cervical, does this criterion about inoperable primary cervical cancer apply to your situation?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, that criterion does not apply to me because my original cancer was endometrial, not cervical.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since your cancer was endometrial, does this criterion about locally advanced cervical cancer apply to you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, that criterion does not apply to me because my cancer is endometrial, not cervical.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have a diagnosis of lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have a diagnosis of lung cancer. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any symptoms caused by cancer in your airways (endobronchial component), such as coughing up blood or shortness of breath?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have a chronic dry cough, but it has improved. I don't know if it's caused by cancer in my airways or if I'm coughing up blood.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told that your lung function is poor, or that your cancer has spread to your lungs (distant lung metastasis)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my lung function is poor or if the cancer has spread to my lungs. My records mention liver lesions and lymph node involvement, but I haven't seen any mention of lung metastasis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Does your medical diagnosis include breast cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have a diagnosis of breast cancer. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with infiltrating ductal carcinoma or ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have a diagnosis of infiltrating ductal carcinoma or DCIS. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently receiving or have you recently received high-dose radiation (HDR) as a boost or accelerated partial breast irradiation?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not received high-dose radiation like that. My treatments have been chemotherapy and immunotherapy, such as carboplatin, paclitaxel, bevacizumab, pembrolizumab, and lenvatinib.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with prostate cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have a diagnosis of prostate cancer. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with localized prostate cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have a diagnosis of prostate cancer. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any memory or thinking problems that make it hard for you to understand study information and give consent?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have memory or thinking problems. I am able to understand information and give consent.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently receiving any investigational chemotherapy drugs as part of another study or treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not currently receiving any investigational chemotherapy drugs. I was taken off my previous treatment for progression in October 2022 and have not started a new study drug since then.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any chemotherapy in the 5 days before your brachytherapy treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't received chemotherapy in the last 5 days. I was taken off my previous treatment in October 2022 and haven't started any new chemo since then.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breast-feeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am 65 years old, so I am not pregnant or breast-feeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any serious ongoing health issues, such as significant heart, lung, liver, or kidney problems, or serious infections, that might make it hard to tolerate this treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have some health issues like hypertension, hypothyroidism, and osteoporosis, but I don't know if I have serious heart, lung, liver, or kidney problems that would prevent me from tolerating this. I do have liver lesions from my cancer, but I'm not sure if that counts as a serious liver problem for this trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us clarify, have you ever been diagnosed with a serious heart, lung, liver, or kidney condition, or had a serious infection in the last 6 months? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a serious heart, lung, liver, or kidney condition. I have liver lesions from my cancer, but I haven't been diagnosed with a separate serious condition in those organs. I also had fevers and chills recently, but I'm not sure if that counts as a serious infection.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any concerns about being able to follow the study schedule and treatment instructions as planned, such as issues with transportation or remembering appointments?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I will have issues with transportation or remembering appointments. I am able to remain on my feet throughout the day, but I have worsening fatigue and feel winded with daily activities.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand better, do you think you will be able to attend all study visits and take medications exactly as scheduled, or do you have specific concerns about keeping up with the treatment plan?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I can commit to the exact schedule. I have worsening fatigue and feel winded with daily activities, which makes me unsure about keeping up with all the visits.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking any blood thinners (anti-coagulation therapy), or have you been told you have abnormal bleeding times?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I am taking blood thinners or have abnormal bleeding times. My medication list includes propranolol and atorvastatin, but I don't see any anticoagulants listed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by a doctor that your anatomy or a tumor might make it difficult or unsafe to insert the brachytherapy device (the tool used to deliver radiation) properly?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my anatomy or tumor makes it difficult to insert the device. I had a hysterectomy, so my uterus is gone, but I have liver lesions and lymph node involvement.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by your doctor that your breast cancer is in multiple areas (multicentric) or that it would be difficult to remove all of it with clear margins?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, that does not apply to me because I do not have breast cancer. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with an autoimmune disorder, such as lupus (SLE) or scleroderma?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have an autoimmune disorder like lupus or scleroderma. My medical history lists hypertension, hiatal hernia, high cholesterol, hypothyroidism, osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis, but I haven't been diagnosed with an autoimmune condition.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by your doctor that your cancer has spread to distant organs or tissues, such as the liver or lungs, beyond the original site?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my cancer has spread to distant organs. I have new liver lesions and lymph node involvement, which is why it is stage M1.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
